 Falklands row erupts as Argentine government slams Princess Anne
 Sophia Papamavroudi Updated 2026년 11월 19일 목 오후 3:46 UTC 0 Princess Anne at Port Stanley, Falkland Islands (Image: Getty) A diplomatic dispute has arisen over the Falkland Islands after the Argentine government formally denounced Princess Anne 's royal visit as a "provocation." The Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Buenos Aires issued a statement condemning the official engagements of King Charles's sister, who is currently touring South Georgia and the Falkland Islands .
 In her role as the Patron of the South Georgia Heritage Trust (SGHT), the Princess Royal travelled to South Georgia from Monday, November 9 to Friday, November 20. Anne's visit will allow her to see the Trust's work to preserve and protect the island's environment and heritage.
 She will also commemorate the life and achievements of polar explorer Sir Ernest Shackleton (1874-1922), who sailed 1,500km in a lifeboat to South Georgia to seek help for his crew after their Antarctic expedition was beset by ice. Anne is joined by her husband, Vice Admiral Sir Tim Laurence.
 The Argentine government stated that the Princess Royal's activities were taking place under what it described as the "illegal British occupation" of the Falklands, South Georgia, the South Sandwich Islands, and surrounding maritime spaces.
 Princess Anne continued her heritage tour, which includes unveiling a memorial to polar explorer Sir Ernest Shackleton and opening the restored Stromness Managers' Villa.
 The commemorative trip has drawn criticism from President Javier Milei's administration, which is linking the royal visit to the ongoing dispute over oil exploration in the South Atlantic.
 Princess Anne speaks with Emma Goss while visiting Cape Pembroke (Image: Getty) Princess Anne visits the Atlantic Conveyor Memorial (Image: Getty) The Argentine Foreign Ministry's statement accused the UK of the "unilateral, illegal exploitation of hydrocarbons through the granting of illegitimate licenses."
 Tensions have increased as the UK advances the Sea Lion oil project, a major drilling venture led by British and Israeli firms. Argentina has brought the dispute to the International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea in Hamburg, requesting an immediate halt to the drilling.
 In addition to its protests, Buenos Aires used the royal visit to renew its demands that London reopen sovereignty negotiations over the archipelago, which Argentina refers to as the Malvinas.
 Despite the ongoing diplomatic tensions, Princess Anne has continued with her official duties.
 Buckingham Palace has stated that the trip, which concludes on November 20, is strictly a commemorative and heritage visit.
 The UK Government continues to reject sovereignty talks, supported by the results of a 2013 referendum in which 99.8 % of Falkland Islanders voted to remain a UK Overseas Territory.
